outcomes.text: Start from a design situation and identify a problem that needs solving.
Analyse the need for a solution.
Inquire into the nature of the problem through research.
Write a detailed specification that drives the development of a solution.
Develop feasible design ideas and choose a solution.
Present the chosen solution.
Plan the creation of the chosen solution.
Follow the plan to create a prototype good enough for testing and evaluation.
Create a model, prototype, product or system as the solution.
Design tests to evaluate the solution.
Carry out the tests and objectively evaluate how successful the solution is.
Identify areas where the solution could be improved.
Explain how the solution will affect the client or target audience.
Use key concepts such as communication, communities, development and systems to frame design inquiry.
Use related design concepts such as adaptation, ergonomics, sustainability and innovation.
Explore design through global contexts: identities and relationships, orientation in space and time, personal and cultural expression.
Explore design through global contexts: scientific and technical innovation, globalization and sustainability, fairness and development.
Explain the role of design in historical and contemporary contexts.
Recognise responsibilities when making design decisions and taking action.
Use technology effectively to access, process and communicate information, model and create solutions.
